propositions: When an author fixes only the named instance the reviewer cited rather than enumerating the entire population it belongs to, the same criterion fires repeatedly across successive passes with different members of that population.
Existing move 12 (Generalize) is always-applicable but carries no proof obligation, so authors can claim completeness without actually achieving it.

A new scoped move (15) must reframe named instances as population samples and require a machine-checkable acceptance criterion (e.g., grep expecting zero matches) that provably fails if any instance remains.
The new move must apply only to criteria where a population actually exists: G1G2, E4, G6, and A1; it must not apply to verifiability criteria like E6 or F1.
The new move registry entry must specify an exact template with a single {subject} placeholder, declare its four trigger criteria via applies_when, and be mirrored in the documentation move table.
